newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Britain says Rifkind won't cut short HK visit.
newsitem.headline: Britain says Rifkind won't cut short HK visit.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind has no plans to cut short his visit to Hong Kong to get back to London for a key parliamentary vote, a senior British official said on Friday.
Rifkind, in Singapore for a meeting of Asian and European foreign ministers, was due to fly to Hong Kong on Saturday before returning home on Tuesday.

If he sticks to his schedule, he will miss an important parliamentary vote on Monday. Prime Minister John Major's beleaguered Conservative administration needs all available hands present for the vote, which should be close.
The vote was called by the opposition Labour Party over Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg's handling of the "mad cow" crisis.

The European Union imposed a ban on British beef exports last year after Britain said it may be possible for people to contract the human form of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) from eating beef. BSE is a fatal brain disease in cattle.
A senior British official said Rifkind did not intend to alter his plans.
"We are going ahead with the visit to Hong Kong," he said. "There no plans at the moment to cut short the visit."
The Conservatives have the same number of parliamentary seats as all opposition parties combined, although they have 51 seats more than second-place Labour.
If Labour were to win the vote, Hogg would be forced to resign and a vote of no-confidence in Major's government could be triggered.
Even if he were to win a no-confidence vote, Major's precarious position would worsen. Labour is 15-20 points ahead in opinion polls and Major must hold a general election by May 22.
He is believed to favour May 1 but might be forced to hold an earlier poll.
If other opposition parties promise to back Labour in Monday's vote, Major would have to ensure that all his members of parliament, even those who are ill or abroad, turn up to vote.
